page: Google Cloud Platform x4-480-8t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized compute instance designed for extreme-scale data operations. It is provisioned on the x86_64 architecture with 480 dedicated vCPUs and an expansive 8192 GB (8 TB) of system memory. This architecture yields approximately 17.07 GB of RAM per vCPU, placing it far above standard compute ratios and tailoring it specifically to workloads requiring massive working memory sets.

The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local storage. Consequently, storage solutions must be mapped externally using networked persistent disks. Hardware virtualization overhead is bypassed entirely due to its bare-metal configuration, giving applications direct hardware-level access across all dedicated CPU cores and the vast unified memory space.

In terms of operational tradeoffs, the absence of bundled local storage places an emphasis on external I/O architecture. Cost efficiency is driven by memory density, allowing enterprise consolidation of sprawling infrastructure into a single bare-metal deployment. Google Cloud Platform x4-480-8t-metal is engineered primarily for large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive enterprise data warehousing, and heavy analytics environments requiring sustained multi-terabyte working sets.
description: Google Cloud Platform x4-480-8t-metal is a high-capacity bare-metal instance situated in the memory-optimized server family. Powered by an x86_64 CPU architecture, it features 480 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 8192 GB of total system RAM, delivering approximately 17.07 GB of memory per processing core. The server includes no GPUs and lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistence. By operating directly on bare metal without hypervisor mediation, it provides unconstrained access to dedicated compute and memory. This hardware profile optimizes infrastructure density for memory-bound applications rather than storage-local caching. It is purpose-built for massive in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise resource planning systems, data warehousing, and extensive analytics tasks requiring multi-terabyte active working memory footprints.
